questions.question: The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas (2nd century BCE to 3rd century CE) is known in Indian history as the __________ period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Post — Mauryan.
  • The Post-Mauryan period saw the rise of dynasties like the Shungas, Kanvas, Satavahanas, and Indo-Greeks.
  • It was a period of significant trade growth with the Roman Empire.
  • This era preceded the 'Golden Age' of the Guptas.

questions.question: Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were in __________ language and were written in the _________ script.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Prakrit, Brahmi.
  • Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were written in the Prakrit language (common tongue).
  • The script used was primarily Brahmi.
  • In the North-West, some inscriptions were in Kharosthi, Greek, and Aramaic.

questions.question: In the Indian subcontinent, the beginning of settlement at Mehrgarh started about_____ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8000.
  • Mehrgarh is one of the earliest sites with evidence of farming and herding, dating back to 8000 years ago (6000 BCE).
  • It is located in Balochistan, Pakistan.
  • People here grew wheat and barley and reared cattle, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raja Rammohun Roy.
  • He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 in Calcutta.
  • He is known for his efforts to abolish Sati (achieved in 1829).
  • He is often called the 'Father of Indian Renaissance'.

questions.question: Who is known as the Prince of Patriots?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.
  • Subhash Chandra Bose was called the 'Prince of Patriots' by Mahatma Gandhi.
  • He founded the Forward Bloc and took command of the Indian National Army (INA).
  • His famous slogan was 'Jai Hind' and 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'.

questions.question: Which Mauryan Indian emperor is renowned for his edicts and pillars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ashoka.
  • Emperor Ashoka is famous for his Major and Minor Rock Edicts and Pillar Edicts.
  • These edicts spread his message of Dhamma (righteousness).
  • His Lion Capital at Sarnath is the National Emblem of India.

questions.question: The partition of Bengal took place in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1905.
  • The Partition of Bengal was carried out by Lord Curzon in 1905.
  • It was officially justified as an administrative necessity but was aimed at dividing the nationalist movement.
  • The partition was annulled in 1911 during the Delhi Durbar.

questions.question: The Gautama Buddha taught in the language of the ordinary people, __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Prakrit.
  • Buddha used Prakrit (specifically Magadhi/Pali dialects) because it was the language of the masses.
  • This helped his teachings of Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path spread rapidly.
  • Jaina Tirthankaras also primarily used Prakrit.

questions.question: Who was the teacher of Chandragupta Maurya of the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kautilya.
  • Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta) was the teacher and prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya.
  • He is the author of the famous treatise on statecraft, the Arthashastra.
  • He played a vital role in the destruction of the Nanda Dynasty.

questions.question: In which year was the Interim government formed at the Centre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1946.
  • The Interim Government of India was formed on September 2, 1946.
  • It was tasked with assisting the transition of India from British rule to independence.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru served as the Vice President of the Executive Council.

questions.question: ___________, (born c. 350 BC—died c. 290), ancient Greek historian and diplomat, is author of Indica.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Megasthenes.
  • Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
  • His book Indica provides a detailed account of the Mauryan administration and society.
  • The original book is lost, but fragments survive in the works of later Greek writers.

questions.question: __________ founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers’ Society) in 1873.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jyotiba Phule.
  • He founded Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to fight for the rights of lower castes and women.
  • He wrote the famous book Gulamgiri (Slavery).
  • He and his wife Savitribai were pioneers of women's education in India.

questions.question: The Veda Samaj was established in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madras.
  • The Veda Samaj was established in Madras (Chennai) in 1864.
  • It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and worked against caste distinctions and for widow remarriage.
  • Chembeti Sridharalu Naidu was a prominent leader who translated Brahmo literature into Telugu and Tamil.

questions.question:
Identify the ancient site from the information given below:

This is an old site with caves and rock shelters. People chose these natural caves because they provided shelter from the rain, heat and wind. These rock shelters are close to the Narmada valley.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhimbetka.
  • Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) is famous for its Paleolithic and Mesolithic rock shelters and paintings.
  • It is located near the Narmada Valley.
  • It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site showcasing early human life.

questions.question: How many sanskrit plays were written by Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Three.
  • Emperor Harshavardhana (Pushyabhuti dynasty) was a scholar and author of three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda.
  • His court poet was Banabhatta, who wrote 'Harshacharita'.
  • Harsha was a great patron of the Nalanda University.

questions.question: The system of the mahalwari settlement was devised by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Holt Mackenzie.
  • The Mahalwari Settlement was devised by Holt Mackenzie and came into effect in 1822.
  • The revenue was collected from a 'Mahal' (a village or group of villages) rather than individuals.
  • It was implemented in the North-Western Provinces, Punjab, and parts of Central India.

questions.question: Sadhna S Nair is the second woman officer from the _________ branch of the Indian Air Force (IAF) to attain the esteemed rank of Air Marshal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is medical.
  • Sadhna S Nair became the second woman officer of the Medical branch to reach the rank of Air Marshal.
  • She also made history by becoming the first woman Director General Hospital Services (Armed Forces).
  • This highlights the growing role of women in senior military leadership.

questions.question: The policy of Permanent Settlement was introduced in India in __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1793.
  • The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
  • It was first implemented in Bengal and Bihar.
  • The land revenue was fixed permanently, making Zamindars the owners of the land as long as they paid the fixed amount.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Simuka.
  • Simuka was the founder of the Satavahana Dynasty (also known as Andhras).
  • The dynasty ruled primarily in the Deccan region (Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana).
  • They were famous for issuing lead coins and their patronage of Buddhism and Brahmanism.

questions.question: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed between Congress and Muslim League?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1916.
  • The Lucknow Pact was an agreement reached between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
  • It was a significant step toward Hindu-Muslim unity in the national struggle.
  • In the same session, the Moderates and Extremists of the Congress reunited.

questions.question: The Gupta Empire is often referred to as the "Golden Age of India." Which field of knowledge saw significant advancements during this period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Science, art, literature.
  • The Gupta Empire (4th-6th century CE) is called the Golden Age due to immense progress in culture.
  • Literature flourished with Kalidasa; science with Aryabhata (concept of Zero, Heliocentrism).
  • Art reached its peak with the Ajanta caves and Dashavatara Temple.

questions.question: The famous work "Arthashastra" attributed to which ancient Indian scholar and strategist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chanakya.
  • The Arthashastra is a masterpiece on political science, economics, and military strategy.
  • It was written by Chanakya (Kautilya), the mentor of Chandragupta Maurya.
  • It consists of 15 books (Adhikaranas) and 180 chapters.

questions.question: What is the name of the earliest form of writing known in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indus Script.
  • The Indus Script (found on seals of Harappa and Mohenjodaro) is the earliest form of writing in India.
  • It is undeciphered to this day.
  • It is generally considered Boustrophedon (written from right to left and then left to right).

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jyotirao Phule.
  • (Duplicate question) Jyotirao 'Jyotiba' Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.
  • He campaigned against untouchability and for the upliftment of the Shudras and Ati-Shudras.
  • His wife Savitribai was a co-leader in these reforms.

questions.question: Famous book Arthashastra tells us that the north-west was important for blankets, and ________ for its gold and precious stones during the Mauryan period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is south India.
  • According to the Arthashastra, different regions were famous for specific goods.
  • North-west India was important for blankets (Kambala).
  • South India was prized for its gold and precious stones.
